newsitem.title: FRANCE: BA would inject 440 mln Ffr in Air Liberte - papers.
newsitem.headline: BA would inject 440 mln Ffr in Air Liberte - papers.

text.p: British Airways is prepared to invest 440 million francs ($84.5 million) in Air Liberte to help the insolvent French carrier break even within three years, French newspapers said on Friday.

The British carrier announced on Monday it would bid 25 million francs to buy Air Liberte, which went into receivership on September 26. It plans eventually to merge Air Liberte with its own French airline TAT.
Les Echos said TAT chairman Marc Rochet had told it of BA's investment plan, while the afternoon daily Le Monde cited BA sources.
Rochet described Air Liberte's situation as "catastrophic" and said a turnaround would be difficult, Les Echos reported.
BA's plans led two other French groups to bid for the carrier to create a French rival to Air France's domestic arm Air Inter Europe. Virgin Express said on Wednesday that it, too,would submit a bid.
A decision by the Creteil commercial court is expected soon.
The French bidders are travel company Nouvelles Frontieres in a partnership with Royal Air Maroc and Banque Rivaud and a group led by AOM pilot Fernand Denan.
AOM is among the assets of state-owned Credit Lyonnais slated to be sold as part of a state bailout of the bank.

AOM chairman Alexandre Courvelaire said in an interview with the Figaro Economie on Friday that he had wanted to buy Air Liberte's assets but was asked by the CDR state agency, which groups the Credit Lyonnais assets for sale, not to bid.
"It was their decision and one I regret," Courvelaire said. He said AOM's survival hinges on the creation of domestic rival to Air France.
Nouvelles Frontieres chairman Jacques Maillot's business plan envisages the subsequent purchase of AOM and an eventual merger of AOM and Air Liberte.
Courvelaire said he proposed an alliance with Air Liberte in July but the deal fell through when Air Liberte's owners rejected a proposal for a 600 million franc capital increase.

After Air Liberte went into receivership, Courvelaire said he prepared a bid on AOM's behalf to acquire the bulk of Air Liberte's network. "It was designed to provide a credible French alternative to foreign offers," he said.

British Airways appealed to Brussels to block any bid by AOM for Air Liberte, saying that would constitute an illegal use of state aid. Courvelaire said his bid for Air Liberte's assets -- and not for the company -- would not have broken the rules.

"The sudden emergence of another French offer headed by Banque Rivaud, Air Liberte's principal shareholder who was at the source of the move to receivership, shocked me deeply," Courvelaire was quoted as saying.
He said the Rivaud group's plan to restore the airline, as opposed to BA's buyout plan, would not fully resolve the liability problems.
Groupe Rivaud, which owns 32.3 percent of Air Liberte, would take 75-80 percent under the plan, according to French newspapers.

BA also criticised the "continuation" plan, according to Le Monde, saying it would earmark 400 million francs "toward the past and a cleanup of the liabilities". It said the strategy risked pushing Air Liberte to bankruptcy.

Le Monde previously reported that Prime Minister Alain Juppe was pushing for a domestic buyer for Air Liberte, which owns around a quarter of the landing slots at Orly, Paris's second-largest airport.
-- Paris Newsroom, +33 1 4221 5452 $ = 5.207 French Francs)
